title: In Matthew 6 How Does The Lords Prayer Serve As A Model For Our Own Prayers
paragraphs: The Lord’s Prayer: A Model for Christian Prayer

In Matthew 6:9-13, Jesus provides what is commonly known as "The Lord’s Prayer." This passage forms a foundational model for Christian prayer, not just in its words, but even more significantly in the priorities and attitudes it teaches. Let’s explore how this prayer shapes our understanding and practice of prayer today.
The Context: A Heart Posture Before God
Before giving the Lord’s Prayer, Jesus teaches about the dangers of hypocritical and vain prayer:

And when ye pray, ye shall not be as the hypocrites: for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men... But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thine inner chamber... and pray to thy Father who is in secret... - Matthew 6:5-6 ASV
This underscores that prayer is an intimate, humble conversation with God, not a performance for others.
Line by Line: The Structure and Heart of the Lord’s Prayer
1. Addressing God as Father
Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. - Matthew 6:9 ASV

Jesus invites us to approach God relationally, as a loving Father. This reflects the believer’s adoption into God’s family through faith in Christ (Romans 8:15 ASV). The phrase “Hallowed be thy name” teaches reverence, reminding us that God is holy and worthy of worship.
2. Seeking God’s Kingdom and Will
Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth. - Matthew 6:10 ASV
Prayer is first about aligning our desires with God’s purposes. The focus is not on our will, but on God’s reign and righteousness. This echoes Jesus’ own prayer in Gethsemane (Matthew 26:39 ASV).
3. Daily Dependence
Give us this day our daily bread. - Matthew 6:11 ASV
Jesus instructs us to depend on God for our daily needs, echoing God’s provision of manna in the wilderness (Exodus 16:4 ASV). This teaches trust and contentment, recognizing God as our provider.
4. Confession and Forgiveness
And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. - Matthew 6:12 ASV
Confession is central to prayer. Jesus links our forgiveness from God with our willingness to forgive others, highlighting the transforming power of grace in a believer’s life (Ephesians 4:32 ASV).
5. Spiritual Protection
And bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. - Matthew 6:13 ASV
Recognizing our weakness, we ask for God’s protection from temptation and evil. This acknowledges our need for God’s help to live holy lives (1 Corinthians 10:13 ASV).
The Lord’s Prayer as a Pattern, Not Just Words
While the Lord’s Prayer can be prayed verbatim, its deeper value lies in its structure:
Begin with worship and reverence.
Surrender your will to God’s purposes.
Trust God for your daily needs.
Confess sins and extend forgiveness.
Seek God’s guidance and protection.
This model helps believers keep their prayers God-centered, humble, and faith-filled.
Conclusion: The Heartbeat of Biblical Prayer

The Lord’s Prayer is a timeless template, teaching us to approach God as Father, seek His will, depend on Him, walk in forgiveness, and rely on His protection. It embodies the spirit of true prayer: relationship, reverence, dependence, confession, and surrender.
